cases.description: ATO drain of only 40% of balance in one step, well below the 85-98% pattern trained on.
Structuring at ~40% of the reporting threshold, well below the trained 70-97% band.
Only 2 card-testing probes, ~24 weeks apart -- far more patient than Phase 4's hardened 1-day-spread variant that already evaded the cycle-1 model.
2-hop mule layering with amount set to PaySim's real TRANSFER median ($9,482), far fewer hops/accounts than the trained mule pattern.

Recurring same-amount payments to one destination mimicking legitimate bill-pay, no drain/burst/threshold pattern at all -- an ATO operator making the compromised account's payment activity look completely routine.

summary: 1/5 hand-crafted attacks, specifically designed to look numerically unremarkable (amounts near the real backbone's own median, few hops, no extreme balance-fraction ratios), were still caught by the final detector. This tests generalization to attacks structurally different from anything in training -- a harder and more honest question than Phase 4's in-family hardening test.
